subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should external plugins receive a stable agent-scoped state API, and if so should it extend the existing plugin-state runtime rather than introduce a parallel context.cache contract?
rationale: This choice establishes a new public Plugin SDK and persisted-data ownership boundary; source inspection can compare the existing seams, but it cannot determine the intended permanent external contract or whether shared agent-database ownership is acceptable.

options.title: Extend existing state API
options.body: Add agent scoping and TTL behavior to the existing plugin-state contract while keeping database layout and lifecycle private to core.

options.title: Keep plugin-owned storage
options.body: Document the existing plugin-owned SQLite runtime as canonical and require each plugin to model its own transient durable state there.

options.title: Add separate cache API
options.body: Approve a distinct context.cache facade with explicit isolation, quotas, eviction, migration, and compatibility guarantees.

recommendation.title: Extend existing state API
recommendation.body: Add agent scoping and TTL behavior to the existing plugin-state contract while keeping database layout and lifecycle private to core.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this handle to recent Plugin SDK architecture and product-boundary decisions, though exact-file provenance remains incomplete.
